title: Beef Chow Mein
subtitle: tender sliced beef and crisp-edged noodles tossed with cabbage, carrots and sprouts in a glossy oyster sauce
imageAlt: Stir-fried egg noodles with sliced beef, cabbage, carrot and bean sprouts in a glossy brown sauce on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Soy sauce, oils, sugar, onion, cornstarch

beforeYouStart.text: Slice the beef across the grain as thin as you can; 20 minutes in the freezer makes it easy.
Have everything cut and the sauce mixed before you start; it cooks in minutes.

steps.title: Beef
steps.text: Toss the beef with the 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp cornstarch. Whisk the oyster sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce, brown sugar, water and 1 tsp cornstarch in a cup.

steps.title: Noodles
steps.text: Cook the noodles as the package says, usually 2–3 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water and toss with the sesame oil.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large wok or skillet over high. Sear half the beef in one layer 1–2 minutes, turning once, until browned and 63°C (145°F). Repeat with the rest of the oil and beef. Set aside.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Add the 1 tbsp oil, onion, cabbage and carrots and stir-fry 3 minutes until just tender. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the noodles and sauce and toss 2 minutes with tongs until glossy and starting to crisp. Return the beef, add the bean sprouts and toss 30 seconds more.

fixIt.fix: Rinse them well after cooking and toss with the sesame oil.
Slice thinner across the grain and don't crowd the pan.
Use high heat and cook in batches so it fries instead of steaming.

saleTip: Sirloin goes on sale at No Frills for about $15/kg; bean sprouts are in the produce cooler, about $2 a bag.
swap: Chicken breast strips: stir-fry to 74°C (165°F). Spaghetti boiled and rinsed for lo mein noodles.
leftovers: Reheats well in a hot skillet with a splash of water.
doneness: Beef strips at 63°C (145°F) (Health Canada, beef pieces). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested Cantonese-style beef chow mein methods (The Woks of Life, RecipeTin Eats): cornstarch-coated beef seared on high heat, quick-fried cabbage and carrot, noodles tossed in an oyster-soy sauce.
prepAhead: Slice and season the beef up to 1 day ahead.
Mix the sauce and cut the vegetables up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: In a hot skillet with 1 tbsp water, 3–4 minutes, or covered in the microwave 2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Beef, noodles and cabbage in the sauce; no bean sprouts or carrot.

fancy.note: Crispy pan-fried noodle cake under the beef, restaurant-style.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: after rinsing, press half the noodles into a hot oiled skillet and fry 4 minutes a side until golden and crisp; repeat for 2 noodle cakes.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: leave the noodles out; toss the sauce, beef and sprouts with the vegetables and spoon it over the noodle cakes.

plating: Noodle cake on a platter, beef and vegetables piled on top.

why.0-2: Cornstarch coats the beef so it stays tender and helps the sauce cling.
why.2-0: Oyster sauce brings the savoury-sweet gloss of takeout chow mein.
why.1-5: Cabbage stays crunchy and soaks up the sauce.

funFact: 'Chow mein' comes from the Taishanese for 'stir-fried noodles'; the dish came to North America with Cantonese immigrants in the 1800s.
